title: Rivers and the Salish Sea
subtitle: Why the water does what it does
summary: Where the water goes in western Washington, from a raindrop on the Cascade divide to the tide race at Deception Pass. Half the course is rivers and lakes: floods, groundwater, the brown water of November, and why the bottom of Lake Washington stays cold all summer. The other half is the Sound, with two tides a day of different heights, a layer of river water floating on the salt, and Hood Canal, whose deep water runs short of oxygen. If you live here, most of it can be checked from a bridge or a ferry.

release.note: First version: fourteen lessons from the rain to the beach, and branches on Seattle's waterworks, the Columbia and fieldwork, each with figures you can work. Photos come later.
